_note: Append a new snapshot each time an authority (SINAPROC, MINSA, Presidencia) publishes figures. null = not reported.

snapshots.note: No consolidated official balance yet. Sinaproc director Omar Smith reported 'several injured' (no figure) and damage concentrated in Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos (Chitré, Venao). No deaths confirmed by any authority. At least 1 injured in Penonomé market (El Siglo/Infobae). Claims of trapped people at El Sitio hostel, Playa Venao, unconfirmed.

snapshots.source_name: SINAPROC (deputy director Malitzie Rivera / director Omar Smith), as reported by media
snapshots.note: Sinaproc says no deaths recorded. 'Several' injured were taken to hospitals in the central provinces, but no number was given. As of ~21:30Z no consolidated figures for injured, displaced or damaged homes had been published. Also cited at 16:24 local in El Tiempo's live blog: https://www.eltiempo.com/mundo/latinoamerica/fuerte-terremoto-en-panama-reportan-sismo-de-magnitud-8-0-durante-la-tarde-de-este-viernes-9-de-octubre-hay-alerta-de-tsunami-3592581 . CSS (Social Security) separately reported no injured patients, users or staff in its facilities (La Estrella, existing report u202610092103_4).

snapshots.source_name: SINAPROC / Ministerio de Gobierno — Comunicado Oficial N° 1
snapshots.note: Comunicado Oficial N° 1 (9 Oct 2026; time not stated, recorded 17:58 local): no deaths; 'some people injured' without a total (incl. 15 students with minor injuries at Escuela Alberto Zúñiga, Coclé); no missing persons reported; 47+ aftershocks (IGC-UP). Damage to government buildings, roads, churches, hotels, shops and homes in Azuero, Coclé, Panamá, Darién and Chiriquí; water treatment plants damaged nationwide (Chilibre at 20%).

conflicts: Magnitude: USGS M7.7 (initially 8.0, then 7.6), depth 12.6 km; IGC-UP M7.2 (initially 7.0), depth 4–10 km, located 39 km W/NW of Tonosí; SGC Colombia 7.3 then 8.0.
Epicentre province: USGS names Pitaloza Arriba (AP/Reuters say Herrera); local media cite Tonosí, Los Santos.

Collapsed hotel location: Panamanian media place it in Penonomé (Hotel Dos Continentes); BioBioChile wrongly reported a four-storey hotel in downtown Panama City; es.wikipedia/Infobae also mention a separate partial hotel collapse near Tonosí.
Some outlets (Vanguardia) wrongly call Penonomé the epicentre zone.

Aftershocks: IGC-UP director Néstor Luque reported 46 aftershocks by mid-afternoon (La Estrella); Telemetro says 'more than 40'/'47+'. Largest: USGS M6.6 at 20:25 UTC near Río Grande (Soná), first reported as M6.9 by SGC Colombia and by IGC (Telemetro, '32 km NE of Coiba'). Earlier IGC values of M6.0–6.5 for early aftershocks do not match the USGS catalogue (largest early aftershock M5.8, El Cacao).
PorEsto claims damage to Puente Centenario; El Tiempo video shows only shaking, no damage reported.
Several outlets recycled Sinaproc text from the 10 Aug 2026 Colombia quake ('9:31 a.m. no persons affected') — not applicable to this event.

Injuries: Sinaproc director Omar Smith reported 'several injured' (no figure); the Caja de Seguro Social (15:27 local) said no patients, users or staff were affected in its own facilities. Neither is a national total.
Largest aftershock (20:25 UTC): USGS M6.6, 14 km W of Río Grande (Veraguas); IGC-UP M6.9, 32 km from Coiba; El Tiempo also cites M6.6 8 km NW of Río Grande.
